Solar mini-grids power rural enterprises in Bundelkhand

A two-year pilot in Bundelkhand connected 14 villages to solar mini-grids, replacing diesel pump-sets and kerosene lighting for roughly 1,200 households. The programme paired the hardware with a pay-as-you-go tariff and a local women-run collective that handled metering and fault reporting.

Early results show micro-enterprise electricity use rose 38% year on year, while reported outages fell from weekly to monthly. The study cautions that tariff affordability remains the binding constraint: a third of surveyed households still ration evening usage. Recommendations include a cross-subsidy from commercial to residential connections and a state-backed repair fund.
title: Solar mini-grids power rural enterprises in Bundelkhand

Crop-residue briquetting as a cooking-fuel alternative

This brief evaluates briquettes pressed from rice and wheat residue as a substitute for fuelwood in peri-urban kitchens. Across 6 clusters, briquette adoption cut average cooking time by 18% and reduced indoor particulate exposure during the morning cooking window.

The main barriers were supply seasonality and the upfront cost of an improved cookstove. The authors recommend aggregating residue procurement at the panchayat level and bundling stove finance with existing self-help-group credit lines.
title: Crop-residue briquetting as a cooking-fuel alternative
